newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies to vote on job-creating bills.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies to vote on job-creating bills.

text.p: Two bills aimed at creating more jobs in Brazil's formal economy were due to be put to votes in the Chamber of Deputies later on Tuesday, deputies said.

One bill would create the Temporary Labor Contract, freeing employers from paying some worker contributions. The other would set a single tax for small and micro-sized companies, cutting red tape and encouraging tiny firms to join the formal sector.
The Temporary Labor Contract would enable employers to hire temporary staff for a maximum of two years, paying reduced contributions to a series of worker funds, Dep. Jose Mendonca Filho said.
Brazilian labor law currently does not distinguish between short-term and long-term hirings.

The bill includes safeguards to prevent employers from sacking existing staff and replacing them with new, short-term workers and sets proportional limits on the total number of employees which companies may hire under the new contract.

"I do not consider this bill a panacea for reducing the problem of unemployment...but it is a contribution and one should remember that half of Brazil's workforce is in the informal sector with no rights at all," Mendonca Filho said.

About 30 million Brazilians work in the informal sector. The government floated the idea of the temporary contract earlier this year but the bill was considered too sensitive for approval before October and November's municipal elections.

The second bill due for a vote on Tuesday, to create a single tax for small and micro companies, remained subject to last-minute negotiations between government whips and representatives of Brazil's small business sector.

Dep. Augusto Nardes, one of the sector's representatives in Congress, said he was seeking a reduction in the total tax small companies would pay to between three and eight percent, from the government's recommendation of between five and 10 percent.
The new tax, known as the Simple, would include federal, state and municipal charges and worker contributions.

A presidential decree signed in November and which now has to be approved in Congress, created a five percent federal tax charge for companies earning up to 120,000 reais a year. The tax increases on a sliding scale to seven percent for firms with annual turnover of up to 720,000 reais.
Companies may opt to include municipal and state taxes in their Simple tax payments.

Nardes said one million small companies stood to join the formal economy as a result of the Simple, adding to the sector's recognized 4.5 million small and micro-sized firms which, he said, employ 20 million workers.
